newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan to begin reforms - president.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan to begin reforms - president.

text.p: Pakistan's new caretaker government will launch economic and other reforms during its three-month term, President Farooq Leghari said on Tuesday.

He said in a televised speech there was a general consensus in the country for giving support to what he called a collapsing economy and rectifying an "intolerably defective working of law and order".
"I am directing the caretaker government to begin reforms in its limited period that could determine the direction for the desired change," he said.
Leghari dismissed prime minister Benazir Bhutto early on Tuesday on charges of corruption and misrule, and named Meraj Khalid as interim leader to oversee fresh general elections set for February 3.
Leghari said he would not promise that these reforms would meet "all the requirements for a restoration of the economy and accountability" or give an immediate major relief to people.
"But we will take such principled decisions which would be in the national interest," he said.
Leghari said Khalid's administration would have to fully implement a recent economic management package with the International Money Fund for the restoration of a $600 million standby loan.
The president said he advised the caretakers to practice austerity and ordered the abolition of luxury VIP lounges at airports for dignitaries.
He promised to hold elections on time and asked people to elect "honest, able, experienced and God-fearing people".

In foreign policy, he said the caretakers would continue a policy of neutrality among warring factions in neighbouring Afghanistan and work for a broad-based government there acceptable to all parties.
He said Islamabad would also continue what he called moral and diplomatic support for Moslem militants fighting Indian ruler over two thirds of the disputed Himalayan region of Kashmir.
But he said Pakistan would also explore all possible ways for a peaceful settlement of the dispute, including bilateral talks with India.
